summary: Ustaz Azlan gives a timeline of the Prophet's SAW 13 years in Makkah, then tells the Sahih Bukhari hadith of Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt strangling the Prophet SAW and Abu Bakr rescuing him and being badly beaten, along with the loyalty of Abu Bakr's family and the role of Fatimah bint Al-Khattab. After torture failed, Quraysh sent An-Nadr and Uqbah to Yathrib; the three Jewish questions (the youths of the cave, Dhul-Qarnayn and the spirit) were answered after a 15-night delay through Surah Al-Kahf and Al-Isra'. The ustaz explains the first migration of 15 people to Abyssinia in Rajab of the fifth year, why Abyssinia was strategic, outside Persian power, and the story of Abu Bakr protected by Ibn Ad-Daghinah.
keyPoints: The Prophet SAW called for 13 years in Makkah: three years closed, then open, then torture, boycott, migration to Abyssinia, the Isra' and Mi'raj and the pledges of Aqabah.
Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt strangled the Prophet SAW beside the Kaaba and Abu Bakr pushed him away with words like the believing man of Pharaoh's household.
The opponents of the Prophet SAW were the wicked, the neutral bystanders, and non-Muslims who defended him like Abu Talib.
After a 15-night delay, Allah answered the three Jewish questions through Al-Kahf and Al-Isra' verse 85.
Fifteen people migrated quietly to Abyssinia in Rajab, including Uthman and Ruqayyah; they were not the weak.
The Prophet SAW chose Abyssinia because it was outside Persian power and its king did not oppress.
Abu Bakr gave up his migration when Ibn Ad-Daghinah protected him, then returned that protection.

lessons.title: Tell the categories of opponents apart
lessons.body: Some are wicked, some neutral bystanders and some non-Muslims who defend; do not lump them together.

lessons.title: Be bold in rebuking injustice
lessons.body: Abu Bakr acted when everyone else was a bystander.

lessons.title: Family and friends willing to sacrifice
lessons.body: Umm Khayr and Fatimah helped in secret despite the danger.

lessons.title: Abu Bakr's joy is his parents' Islam
lessons.body: Abu Bakr was happiest when the Prophet SAW was happy and hoped for Abu Talib's Islam.

lessons.title: Say insha'Allah
lessons.body: The delay in revelation after the Prophet SAW forgot insha'Allah teaches reliance on Allah.

lessons.title: Allah answers from several directions
lessons.body: Al-Kahf answers the questions, gives hope and shows the wisdom behind hardship.

lessons.title: Migration is not weakness
lessons.body: Those sent to Abyssinia were strong and influential; the weak could not leave.

lessons.title: Geopolitics in the Prophet's SAW decisions
lessons.body: Abyssinia was chosen as outside Persian power and as a backup plan.

lessons.title: Never give up on anyone
lessons.body: Umar was thought impossible to convert, yet the Prophet SAW prayed for him.

lessons.title: Weak is not fabricated
lessons.body: A weak report may be cited with its status clear; do not equate it with fabricated.

lessons.title: Protection must not muzzle worship
lessons.body: Abu Bakr returned Ibn Ad-Daghinah's protection rather than hide his worship.

dalil.context: A Sahih Bukhari hadith from Urwah, when he asked Abdullah ibn Amr about the harshest thing done to the Prophet SAW.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW was praying beside the Kaaba when Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt put a cloth around his neck and strangled him; Abu Bakr came, pushed Uqbah away and said, 'Would you kill a man because he says my Lord is Allah, when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?'

dalil.context: The words of the believing man of Pharaoh's household, which matched Abu Bakr's.
dalil.translation: A secret believer from Pharaoh’s family said, ‘How can you kill a man just for saying, “My Lord is God”? He has brought you clear signs from your Lord- if he is a liar, on his own head be it- and if he is truthful, then at least some of what he has threatened will happen to you. God does not guide any rebellious, outrageous liar.

dalil.context: Allah answered the question about the spirit: it is my Lord's affair and you were given little knowledge.
dalil.translation: [Prophet], they ask you about the Spirit. Say, ‘The Spirit is part of my Lord’s domain. You have only been given a little knowledge.’

dalil.context: The cave youths took refuge so Allah might open His mercy; linked to the Hijrah. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Now that you have left such people, and what they worshipped instead of God, take refuge in the cave. God will shower His mercy on you and make you an easy way out of your ordeal.’

dalil.context: Allah's earth is wide for emigration and the patient are rewarded without measure.
dalil.translation: Say, ‘[God says], believing servants, be mindful of your Lord! Those who do good in this world will have a good reward- God’s earth is wide––and those who persevere patiently will be given a full and unstinting reward.’

dalil.context: The ustaz stresses not to give up on anyone.
dalil.translation: O Allah, strengthen Islam with whichever of the two Umars is dearer to You.

dalil.context: Aisha's hadith in Sahih Bukhari; the same words Khadijah used for the Prophet SAW.
dalil.translation: You keep family ties, honour guests, help the poor and bear the burdens of the afflicted; a man like you should not leave.

dalil.context: A weak report; the ustaz explains it is weak but not fabricated.
dalil.translation: Uthman is the first to migrate with his family after Prophet Lut AS.
